    # setup edit forms so that only posts created by this user can be selected as

    def edit_form(self, obj):  # type: ignore[override]

        form.featured_post.query_factory = lambda: Post.query.filter(

class PostAdmin(ModelView):
    column_display_pk = True
    column_list = [
        "id",
        "user",
        "user.email",
        "title",
        "date",
        "tags",
        "background_color",
        "created_at",
    ]
    column_editable_list = [
        "background_color",
    ]
    column_default_sort = ("date", True)
    create_modal = True
    edit_modal = True

        "id",
        "title",
        "date",
        "user.email",
        ("user", ("user.last_name", "user.first_name")),  # sort on multiple columns
    ]
    column_searchable_list = [
        "title",
        "tags.name",
        "user.first_name",
        "user.last_name",
    ]
    column_labels = {
        "title": "Post Title",
        "tags.name": "Tags",
        "user.first_name": "User's first name",
        "user.last_name": "Last name",
    }
    column_filters = [
        "id",
        "user.first_name",
        "user.id",
        "background_color",
        "created_at",
        "title",
        "date",
        "tags",

            Post.title,
            "Fixed Title",
            options=(("test1", "Test 1"), ("test2", "Test 2")),

        filters.FilterLike(column="user.email", name="Author Email"),

            column="user.account.provider",

        ),

    can_export = True
    export_max_rows = 1000
    export_types = ["csv", "xls"]

    # Pass arguments to WTForms. In this case, change label for text field to

I couldn't find a bug in the code, so I haven't changed any files. The Internal Server Error is most likely a Flask-Babel setup problem in your app.

**What I found**
- I reproduced this in a scratch script (`$TMPDIR/repro.py`, outside your repo) using a post form with `tags` required via `DataRequired`. I submitted it with no tags.
- With Flask-Babel installed but not initialised on the app, I got a 500. The traceback ends in `KeyError: 'babel'`.
- Flask-Admin translates the "This field is required" message through `flask_babel`. That fails if no `Babel(app)` was created, and the failure only shows up when a validation error has to be rendered. That's why saving with tags selected works fine.
- With `Babel(app)` added, the same request returns 200 and the form shows "This field is required".

**The fix**
Initialise Flask-Babel in your app, as `examples/sqla/admin/__init__.py:25` does and `doc/advanced.rst` describes:

```python
from flask_babel import Babel
babel = Babel(app)
```

If you don't want translations, uninstall `flask_babel`. Flask-Admin then falls back to plain English messages.

**What I couldn't confirm**
Your app isn't in this repo; it only has the Flask-Admin library and its examples. I haven't seen your admin setup or your real traceback, so I'm inferring the cause from the reproduction. If you still get a 500 after adding `Babel(app)`, paste the traceback from your server log and I'll look again.
